title: Tools That Reshape Their Users
sentences: We tend to describe a tool as something that simply extends an intention we already had.
The account is flattering to its users and only intermittently true in ordinary practice.
A tool that is easy in one direction quietly makes that direction feel obvious.
Over time the obvious direction becomes the one we take without ever deciding to take it.
Writing by hand and writing at a keyboard reliably produce recognisably different prose.
Neither is superior, but pretending that the two are equivalent is careless.
The interesting question is never whether a given tool is good or bad for us in the abstract.
It is which of our existing habits the tool quietly makes cheaper than all the others.
Cheapness, repeated daily across years, does the work that argument never manages to do.
By the time we notice the change, we have usually lost the ability to make any useful comparison.
